The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will enable a series of measurements at unprecedented energies and luminosities, providing new opportunities to investigate the microscopic structure of nucleons and nuclei at small $x_B$. Exclusive processes such as Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering (DVCS) offer unique access to the three-dimensional structure of hadrons through Generalized Parton Distributions (GPDs), while polarized electron and ion beams further enable detailed studies of spin-dependent structure. A model for coherent DVCS on polarized $^3$Heis developed and applied to simulations of for $9\times166$-GeV $e^3$He collisions at the EIC. Using this framework, the statistical precision achievable is estimated for measurements of beam-spin asymmetries and for the extraction of the Compton Form Factors (CFFs) $\mathcal H_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ and $\tilde{\mathcal H}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$. Early EIC data are found to enable precise differential measurements of the unpolarized CFF $\mathcal H_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ and to provide significant constraints on its real and imaginary components. By contrast, meaningful constraints on the polarized CFF $\tilde{\mathcal H}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ require substantially larger integrated luminosities. The kinematics of the recoil $^3$He nucleus are also examined, and the advanced far-forward detector capabilities at the EIC required to tag the intact nucleus and perform fully exclusive measurements of coherent nuclear DVCS are discussed.
♻ ☆ Chiral QCD phase in equilibrium with Hadron Gas and the location of the critical point
N. G. Antoniou, F. K. Diakonos, A. S. Kapoyannis
We develop a description of the equation of state of QCD matter with restored chiral symmetry, which is in thermal and chemical equilibrium with the hadronic phase. The hadron gas is described with thermodynamically consistent volume corrections. The chiral phase is composed of a set of few quark condensates, each of which corresponds to a family of hadrons with specific quark content. On the boundary between the two phases we apply the requirement of conservation of particle numbers per family. We use lattice calculations for temperatures below the transition curve to determine hadronic volumes. We find that the pion system plays decisive role in the shift of the transition from higher order (crossover) to first order. For four volume models and five hadron sets we calculate the location of the critical point as function of critical temperature $T_c$ at vanishing baryon density. Among other acceptable solutions, if we additionally impose the equality between the densities of quarks contained in mesons and baryons, we find a critical point residing in the interval of baryon chemical potential $μ_B \simeq$ 234-279 MeV and of temperature $T \simeq$ 148-156 MeV. We propose as signal of approach to the critical point the determination of the chiral pion mass through experimentally measured pion multiplicities in heavy-ion collisions.

♻ ☆ Nuclear pasta in hot neutron-star matter and proto-neutron stars
Jian Zhou, Junbo Pang, Hong Shen, Jinniu Hu
We investigate nuclear pasta phases appearing in hot neutron-star matter based on the compressible liquid-drop model, where the matter consists of a dense liquid phase and a dilute gas phase separated by a sharp interface. The surface tension is calculated self-consistently from the Thomas-Fermi approximation, and it depends on temperature and isospin asymmetry. We employ relativistic mean-field (RMF) models with different symmetry energy slopes to describe nuclear interactions. It is found that the RMF models with smaller symmetry energy slopes result in various pasta phases at low temperatures, whereas those with larger symmetry energy slopes yield only the droplet configuration up to the crust-core transition density. We examine the occurrence and influence of pasta phases in proto-neutron stars with a constant entropy per baryon. These pasta phases may occur in the inner crust and play an important role in the thermal evolution of the star.

This approach neglects uncertainty in the medium and prevents hard observables from providing additional constraints on its properties. We investigate these effects in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76$ TeV using sequential Bayesian inference in a reduced three-parameter space. We vary the initial normalization and nucleon width of the medium together with the jet--medium coupling, combining JETSCAPE medium evolution with MATTER+LBT calculations of high-$p_T$ hadron and inclusive-jet suppression. We first constrain all three parameters using the hard observables alone, then incorporate a projected soft-sector posterior through sequential inference. We find that the hard observables are sensitive to the medium properties and reveal substantial correlations with the jet--medium coupling, reflecting their compensating effects on jet quenching. Propagating the soft-sector information shifts the preferred coupling relative to a fixed-medium extraction, with the update driven primarily by hadron-suppression measurements. Despite substantial differences in the medium parameters and coupling favored by hard-observable-only and sequential inference, their suppression predictions remain similar over much of the measured range. These findings highlight the difficulty of distinguishing changes in the QGP medium from changes in microscopic jet--medium interaction strength using inclusive suppression measurements alone.

♻ ☆ Uncovering the mechanism of chiral three-nucleon force in driving spin-orbit splitting
Tokuro Fukui, Giovanni De Gregorio, Angela Gargano
The three-nucleon force (3NF) is crucial in shaping the shell structure of atomic nuclei, particularly impacting the enhancement of spin-orbit (SO) splitting, especially in nuclei with significant deviations from stability. Despite its importance, the specific mechanisms driving this enhancement remain unclear. In this study, we introduce a decomposition scheme based on the rank of irreducible tensors forming the 3NF, derived from chiral effective field theory at next-to-next-to-leading order, to elucidate their influence on SO splitting. Within the shell-model framework, our analysis reveals that the rank-1 component of the 3NF is the primary factor enlarging the energy gap between the $0p_{3/2}$ and $0p_{1/2}$ single-particle levels in $p$-shell nuclei. Since the rank-1 component originates exclusively from the $2π$-exchange 3NF, our finding will not depend on the choice of the low-energy constants of contact terms. We also remark on the antisymmetry of the rank-1 3NF, which can affect the quantum entanglement of spin states. This study lays the groundwork for further exploration into this field toward a microscopic understanding of the 3NF impact on the nuclear shell structure.

☆ Ohmic warm inflation
Anish Ghoshal, Alessandro Strumia
We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflaton velocity becomes a five-dimensional electric field and friction becomes Ohmic dissipation, which seems able to sustain warm inflation compatibly with observations.

☆ Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
Gabriela Barenboim, Stephen J. Parke, Alberto Sánchez Vargas
It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($δ$) is 0 or $π$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $ν_μ$ and $ν_τ$, but not the $ν_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sinδ$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. The confusion arises from an improper T test that subtracts a probability from itself: a mathematical identity, not a physics result. In this paper, we clarify the distinctions between a proper and an improper T test as well as the proper and improper CP and CPT tests, for a general, arbitrary matter profile. For a toy model consisting of two different layers of constant density, we find that the maximum T-violation is obtained when one layer is close to the solar resonance, and the other is close to the atmospheric resonance. We address whether the matter asymmetry for DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments is sufficiently large to allow the $\sinδ$ dependence to be probed in $ν_μ$ survival probability. We also discuss future experimental scenarios that could probe T/CP-violation in $ν_μ$ survival probability.

In practice this integral is cut off at momenta not far above the chemical potentials being probed. We evaluate it exactly, at an arbitrary cutoff, using the Hermite reduction. The result is an algebraic boundary term and three incomplete elliptic integrals, one of each kind. Their modulus, parameter and amplitude at the end of the path are fixed by the triangle formed by the two levels at zero momentum. The power divergences reside in the boundary term, while the remaining divergence is logarithmic: the momentum axis is an open path on an elliptic curve, and the ultraviolet is the puncture at which it ends. The closed form makes the role of regularization explicit. As the cutoff is removed, sharp and smooth cutoffs acting on the momentum alone differ only by an additive constant and by two terms that the vacuum inputs fix. The medium separation scheme reproduces the resulting potential up to an additive constant. By contrast, a cutoff applied separately to the two levels generates an isospin density below the onset of condensation and violates the Silver Blaze property. The closed form gives the state that continues the vacuum along the isospin axis without numerical momentum integration. With the same vacuum fit, a cutoff kept finite gives a visibly different state. The two differ by explicit terms that vanish only as the cutoff is removed: they are different models, not two regularizations of one.

In this framework, the light neutrino masses are suppressed by the extended seesaw parameter, $μ$, thereby allowing for $\mathcal{O}(10\, \mathrm{TeV})$ right-handed (RH) neutrinos, while avoiding small Yukawa couplings as in other neutrino mass models and near degeneracies in the RH neutrino spectrum as required by the low-scale leptogenesis paradigm. Contributions to the $0 νββ$-decay rate from additional sterile neutrinos can be appreciable, while the corresponding contributions to the early universe lepton asymmetry washout rate are suppressed by other parameters not entering the $0 νββ$-decay amplitudes. We show that for keV-MeV scale, sterile neutrinos future ton-scale $0νββ$-decay experiments offer potential signals while maintaining viable leptogenesis.

♻ ☆ Two-Dimensional Transverse-Momentum Subtraction and Semi-Inclusive Deep-Inelastic Scattering at N$^3$LO in QCD
Liang Dong, Shen Fang, Jun Gao, Hai Tao Li, Ding Yu Shao, Hua Xing Zhu, Yu Jiao Zhu
Identified hadron production is essential for the study of nucleon structure and QCD hadronization at high energies. We present the first calculation of unpolarized semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS) at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N$^3$LO) in perturbative QCD. Our calculation is based on a novel method of two-dimensional transverse-momentum subtraction motivated by QCD factorization of soft and collinear singularities. The N$^3$LO corrections are moderate in general but can be significant in threshold regions, and exhibit excellent perturbative convergence and reduced scale variations. The fully differential framework allows for arbitrary selection cuts and directly enables precision nucleon tomography at the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider, establishing the theory foundation needed to match the anticipated experimental accuracy. Generalization of the method to calculations of polarized SIDIS is also feasible.
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, published version
♻ ☆ The Majoron Cosmological Window: Dark Matter and Thermal Leptogenesis
Arturo de Giorgi, Daniel Naredo-Tuero, Xavier Ponce Díaz
The majoron is the Nambu-Goldstone boson associated with the spontaneous breaking of a global $B-L$ symmetry. Remarkably, the minimal majoron framework can simultaneously address three key empirical indications of physics beyond the Standard Model: neutrino masses, the matter-antimatter asymmetry, and dark matter. In this work, we identify the cosmologically viable region in which majoron dark matter and high-scale thermal leptogenesis can be realised simultaneously. We show that successful leptogenesis plays a central role in making this scenario predictive: by constraining the right-handed-neutrino mass scale, it determines the irreducible freeze-in contribution to the majoron abundance and fixes the size of the couplings relevant for visible dark matter decays. Combining the irreducible dark matter production mechanisms with warm dark matter limits and indirect searches for decaying dark matter, we map the resulting majoron cosmological window and show that future X- and gamma-ray telescopes can probe part of the surviving parameter space.

♻ ☆ Thermal Gauge Theory for a Rotating Plasma
Alberto Salvio
This paper provides a systematic and complete study of thermal gauge theory for generic equilibrium density matrices, which feature arbitrary values not only of temperature and chemical potentials, but also of average angular momentum. This work extends previous studies, which focused on pure scalar-fermion theories, to all gauge theories coupled to an arbitrary matter sector. Path-integral methods are developed to study ensemble averages and thermal Green's functions of general operators, with an arbitrary number of points, in all interacting gauge theories. These methods cover both the real-time and imaginary-time formalisms. Generalized Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) conditions are obtained both in coordinate and in momentum space for operators in general representations of the Lorentz and internal symmetry group. This allows us to obtain all thermal propagators including those of gauge fields and Faddeev-Popov ghosts. By analyzing all interactions in detail, it is shown that, in perturbation theory, only the propagators are affected by the average angular momentum and the chemical potentials, the vertices remain unmodified. The paper presents fully model-independent results and can, therefore, be applied to any specific thermal field theory.
comment: 24 pages. v2: detailed analysis of the cylindrical plasma case, more explanations and references added; v3: typos fixed and more clarifications added, journal version
♻ ☆ Threshold resummation for top-quark pair production in association with a jet at the LHC
Bakar Chargeishvili
We study threshold resummation for the invariant-mass distribution of a top-quark pair and a jet at the LHC. We perform the resummation at next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy in soft-collinear effective theory, with the logarithms of the jet radius treated at fixed order, and match it to the exact next-to-leading-order (NLO) cross section. We correct the one-loop soft anomalous-dimension matrices in the literature and validate the hard functions. We compare the leading-power kernel with exact real emission, and validate this comparison on Drell-Yan production. At invariant masses up to about 1 TeV with a fixed jet threshold the method does not apply. At 1-4 TeV with a jet threshold of 15% of the invariant mass, the kernel describes the exact real-emission density close to threshold but fails once the emitted energy exceeds about 100-200 GeV. We trace part of this failure to initial states absent from the kernel, which depend on $τ=M^2/S$, with $M$ the invariant mass and $\sqrt{S}$ the hadronic centre-of-mass energy. In addition, at fixed $τ$ the difference between the kernel and the exact result grows with the ratio $M/m_t$ of the invariant mass to the top-quark mass. As a consequence, the resummed correction beyond NLO, for a scale equal to the invariant mass, ranges from 1-2% to 17-23% for different treatments of this region. The upper end becomes 13-16% for a jet threshold of 20% of the invariant mass and 23-33% for 10%. The range is not a bound, and the correction is not under perturbative control. We therefore keep NLO as the central prediction. We compare the possible effect of resummation with the NLO scale uncertainty, with the known next-to-next-to-leading-order corrections, and with NLO matched to a parton shower.
♻ ☆ Matching second-order classical and 1-loop quantum tensor power spectra in de Sitter spacetime
A. Hauser, M. Laine
Large corrections to the inflationary tensor power spectrum have been speculated to emerge either as second-order scalar-induced classical effects, or as 1-loop quantum corrections. These two sources are not independent of each other. Choosing the example of a massless minimally coupled scalar field, we show how the full 1-loop result can be divided into its classical and vacuum parts. Working first in dimensional regularization, we show that the classical part is IR divergent, with IR referring to small comoving momenta that have an influence for a very long time. In the full 1-loop quantum result, these divergences cancel. Introducing then a momentum cutoff that permits for a numerical evaluation of the classical contribution, we show that the IR sensitivity manifests itself as a cubic divergence. We suggest a procedure of "non-perturbative renormalization" for extracting physical information not affected by the divergence. If this can be implemented in realistic systems, it could consolidate numerical studies of inflationary scalar-induced gravitational waves.

♻ ☆ Electromagnetic pion mass splitting using a Pauli-Villars-regulated photon propagator
Alessandro De Santis, Dominik Erb, Harvey B. Meyer
We present a lattice QCD calculation of the charged-neutral pion mass splitting $M_{π^+} - M_{π^0}$ at $\mathcal{O}(α_\mathrm{em})$ using a recently proposed framework based on a Pauli-Villars (PV) regulated photon propagator defined in the continuum and infinite-volume limit, with $Λ$ acting as an additional UV cutoff scale. This formulation, when combined with a dedicated treatment of the elastic contribution, avoids power-law finite-volume effects on electromagnetic mass shifts. We perform the calculation using CLS ensembles, studying finite-volume effects, the continuum limit and the extrapolation to the physical point for several values of the scale $Λ$. By means of the Cottingham formula, we further decompose the result into elastic and inelastic contributions at fixed $Λ$. Our final result, after removing the cutoff scale $Λ$, is $M_{π^+} - M_{π^0} = 4.56(22)$ MeV, in good agreement with the experimental measurement. Our complete calculation demonstrates that, for a mass splitting not requiring any counterterms, the formalism can be implemented successfully, whilst also offering useful insights into the computation of electromagnetic corrections to other observables.
comment: 32 pages, 13 figures, 5 tables. Revised version accepted for publication in JHEP
♻ ☆ Shape wall: Constraints on late-time solutions to the Hubble tension from the dimensionless expansion rate
Miguel A. Sabogal, Luis A. Escamilla, Davide Pedrotti, Edvig Selimaj, Sunny Vagnozzi
The standard "no-go theorem" against late-time solutions to the Hubble tension is essentially a normalization wall, since Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) measurements constrain the product $H_0r_d$, with $r_d$ the sound horizon at baryon drag. However, late-time solutions (which keep $r_d$ fixed) are tightly constrained not only by the BAO normalization $H_0r_d$, but also by the shape of the expansion history, i.e. the dimensionless expansion rate $E(z) \equiv H(z)/H_0$. We show that, if $r_d$ and the acoustic angular scale $θ_s$ are fixed, an increase in $H_0$ needs to be matched by an equal fractional increase in the dimensionless distance integral $I \equiv \int dz/E(z)$: $δH_0/H_0 \simeq δI/I$. We use this to quantify the "shape wall" set by relative distance constraints on $E(z)$, which we reconstruct nonparametrically, using Gaussian Processes and the latest unanchored Type Ia Supernovae (SNeIa) and BAO data. In our most conservative analysis using PantheonPlus SNeIa and DESI DR2 BAO data, we find a maximum fractional increase in $H_0$ of $\lesssim 2\%$, falling well short of the $\gtrsim 8\%$ required to solve the tension. This shape wall holds even in the presence of early-time new physics, and limits the maximum increase in $H_0$ which can be contributed by late-time modifications to $E(z)$ at fixed $θ_s$. Therefore, late-time modifications, whether invoked alone or alongside early-time new physics, face not only the well-known normalization wall, but also a stringent percent-level shape wall.

♻ ☆ Probing gluon saturation through inclusive hadron production in DIS
Carlisle Casuga, Swaleha Mulani, Heikki Mäntysaari
We investigate gluon saturation effects in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) at small-$x$ within the Color Glass Condensate framework. We compute the SIDIS cross section at leading order in the dipole picture, expressing it in terms of the dipole-target scattering amplitude. We validate our framework by comparing with the charged hadron spectra measured at HERA. Our predictions for the EIC indicate that saturation effects result in significant nuclear suppression in the SIDIS cross section, and can provide complementary constraints on the initial condition for the Balitsky-Kovchegov evolution extracted from inclusive DIS data. These results demonstrate that SIDIS measurements at the EIC are sensitive to nonlinear QCD dynamics in the saturation regime.

♻ ☆ Determining the Proton's Gluon Cloud Geometry from HERA Data
Tobias Toll, Nahid Vasim
This preprint is superseded by arXiv:2609.28700, which corrects the fit uncertainties and updates the dipole-model parameters; numerical results should be taken from that paper. The transverse shape of the proton's small-$x$ gluon distribution is determined from exclusive $J/ψ$ photoproduction at HERA. We derive analytic expressions for the coherent and incoherent diffractive cross sections in the hotspot model at leading twist, enabling a global fit to all 104 available H1 and ZEUS data points, with $|t|<30~{\rm GeV}^2$ and $40\leq W\leq 251~{\rm GeV}$, with $χ^2/{\rm ndf}=0.72$. The gluonic hotspots are resolved into a core of size 0.088(10) fm surrounded by an exponential halo of range 0.20(2) fm, matching the penetration depth of lattice flux tubes. This shape is stable over $\xpom$ and over the assumed number of hotspots in the range $5\leq N_{hs}\leq 12$. We find the Ginzburg-Landau parameter of the QCD vacuum to be $κ=2.7(7)$, which corresponds to fluxtube geometry in a type-II dual superconductor. The calculated QCD string-tension from the extracted parameter values is in agreement with theoretical calculations on the lattice. The gluonic geometry evolves only through a slow transverse diffusion of the hotspot centers with $α'_{\rm eff.}=0.060(19)~{\rm GeV}^{-2}$, while the incoherent cross section at small $|t|$ is dominated by shot-noise fluctuations at the order of a few gluons per hotspot.
comment: 14 pages, 6 figures
♻ ☆ Casimir effect in Gribov-Zwanziger theory
David Dudal, Philipe De Fabritiis, Sebbe Stouten, David Vercauteren
We consider Yang-Mills theory with two infinite parallel plates, separated by a distance \(L\), that are perfect magnetic conductors (PMC) or perfect electric conductors (PEC). Recently, it was shown that the Gribov copy problem persists in such a setting. We then study the Gribov-Zwanziger (GZ) action in the presence of those boundaries using functional integral methods. Lagrange multiplier fields allow one to lift the boundary conditions into the action, after which the boundary modifications to the gluon propagator can straightforwardly be determined. In the PEC case, we provide evidence that, even when translation invariance is (partially) broken, the usual horizon term in the GZ action still restricts the functional integral to the Gribov region. We compute the Casimir energy for GZ with PMC or PEC plates, both directly from the functional integral and from the energy-momentum tensor, obtaining consistent results. We compare our analytical results with recent lattice data, in both 4D and 3D. A priori, one might expect that the boundary-modified gluon propagator introduces new \(L\)-dependencies into the GZ gap equation. This would make the Gribov mass \(γ\) dynamically dependent on \(L\), implying an interesting interplay with the Casimir energy. However, we show that no such dynamical \(L\)-dependence occurs within the current approximation.
comment: 30 pages. Published in PRD
♻ ☆ Phenomenological explorations of a quasi-degenerate $Z'$ boson
C. S. Kim, Donghun Lee, Gyeonghyun Min, Sechul Oh, Dibyakrupa Sahoo
We do a general model-independent phenomenological analysis of the curious case of a quasi-degenerate $Z'$ boson, i.e. a $Z'$ boson whose mass is close to that of the Standard Model (SM) $Z$ boson, with SM $Z$-like fermionic couplings. Assuming that it exists hidden or unresolved in the present experimental data, we show that the experimentally measured invisible width can constrain the coupling of such a $Z'$ to SM fermions. From tree-level calculation alone we show that presence of such a $Z'$ boson affects both the cross-section and forward-backward asymmetry of the process $e^+ e^- \to f \bar{f}$ where $f$ (with $f\neq e^-$) can be a lepton or quark. We also show that the dimensionless difference-over-sum (DoS) ratios of both cross-section and forward-backward asymmetry are more effective observables to probe the $Z'$-pole.
comment: 18 pages, 6 figures
♻ ☆ Impact of non-standard neutrino-electron interactions on Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
Julien Froustey, Stefano Gariazzo, Jaume Moncho, Sergio Pastor, Ofelia Pisanti
Neutrino non-standard interactions (NSI) with electrons, predicted in many extended theoretical models of particle physics, are known to alter the picture of neutrino decoupling from the cosmic plasma. We update previous analyses of neutrino decoupling in the presence of NSI with electrons, extending the parameter space and assessing their impact on the primordial light-element abundances produced during Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN). We show that tracking the NSI-induced modifications of the neutrino distributions is necessary to accurately predict the helium-4 abundance, which cannot be derived from a pure $N_{\rm eff}$-driven change. BBN therefore provides additional observables that are complementary to $N_{\rm eff}$. We then derive cosmological constraints on non-universal and flavour-changing NSI parameters, using different dataset combinations, and compare them with bounds from terrestrial experiments. We find that the cosmological limits are significantly less stringent than the terrestrial ones, but they provide an independent probe of neutrino interactions in the early universe.

♻ ☆ Extracting production fractions of $b$ hadrons from exclusive semi-leptonic decays
Carolina Bolognani, Martin Jung, Méril Reboud, K. Keri Vos
Ratios of production fractions of $b$ hadrons are a dominant source of uncertainty in many LHC analyses, in particular in measurements with $B_s$ mesons. The currently used value for $f_s/f_d$ is based on a combination of hadronic and semi-inclusive semi-leptonic decays, and relies in part on assumptions about the underlying decays that are hard to quantify. We propose an independent alternative method to obtain this quantity by measuring ratios of the exclusive semi-leptonic decays $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(*)} \ell \barν$. This method benefits from significant cancellations of both experimental and theoretical uncertainties, as well as robustness against potential contamination from heavy physics beyond the Standard Model. As a proof of principle, we show that current measurements constrain $f_s/f_d$ with an uncertainty of $7\%$, dominated by present experimental uncertainties. This method can also be applied to other ratios of production fractions involving heavier $b$ hadrons, such as $B_c$ or $Λ_b$.
♻ ☆ Examples of infinitesimal Gribov copies in the presence of planar boundaries, and an emergent boundary gauge invariance in Yang-Mills theory
David Dudal, Luigi Rosa, Sebbe Stouten
First, we explicitly construct zero-modes of the Yang-Mills Faddeev-Popov operator in the presence of two parallel plates, with either perfect electric (PEC) or perfect magnetic (PMC) boundary conditions imposed. This establishes the existence of infinitesimal Gribov copies with finite action, and even finite L_2-norm, in Yang-Mills theory with non-trivial interfaces. We adapt Henyey's construction, although the boundary configuration imposes extra restrictions on the ansatz for the gauge field. Second, we discuss the phenomenon of an emergent boundary gauge invariance for PEC and PMC plates in Yang-Mills theory. This shall be important when applying the Gribov-Zwanziger procedure to parallel plate setups, of relevance for non-perturbatively studying the non-Abelian Casimir effect in the future.

♻ ☆ Imprints of screened dark energy on nonlocal quantum correlations
Fabiano Feleppa, Gaetano Lambiase, Sunny Vagnozzi
We investigate how screening mechanisms, reconciling light scalar fields driving cosmic acceleration with local fifth force constraints, can be probed via their impact on nonlocal quantum correlations between entangled spin pairs, whose evolution on a curved background is affected by General Relativity (GR) and screened modified gravity effects. We consider a gedankenexperiment featuring a pair of massive, spin-$1/2$ particles orbiting the Earth, evaluating their nonlocal correlations through spin observables associated to the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality. Using a general formalism developed earlier for curved space-time spin evolution, we compute the effects of screening on the CHSH inequality, finding its degree of violation to be suppressed relative to the flat space-time case. Applying this formalism to the chameleon, symmetron, and dilaton mechanisms, we identify currently unconstrained regions of parameter space where the screening contribution is comparable to that of GR. While detecting these effects will be challenging, our work provides a proof-of-principle for testing screened dark energy through quantum nonlocality.
comment: 24 pages, 3 figures (6 subfigures in total); v2: typos corrected, references added, accepted for publication in Physical Review D; v3: further typos fixed; v4: minor notational corrections; v5: corrections and updated figures, symmetron and dilaton results revised
♻ ☆ Bounds on screened dark energy from near-Earth space-based measurements
Fabiano Feleppa, Welmoed Marit de Graaf, Philippe Brax, Gaetano Lambiase
We test screened dark energy with near-Earth, space-based measurements. In a post-Newtonian framework, we compute leading corrections to geodetic precession (Gravity Probe B), LAGEOS-2 pericenter advance, and the Sagnac delay in a prospective orbital configuration, yielding bounds on chameleon, symmetron, and dilaton models. LAGEOS-2 sets the strongest Earth-orbit limits on symmetron and dilaton, while a Sagnac setup at the projected sensitivity of state-of-the-art space clocks gives the tightest chameleon constraint. These results show that low-density, space-based experiments sensitively probe screened dark energy and exclude previously allowed parameter space. Notably, at an assumed delay precision of $\mathcal{O}\big(10^{-19}\big)$, a Sagnac test would exclude the entire chameleon parameter space considered.

♻ ☆ Exceptional Jordan spectra and fermion finite selectors and joint quark tests
Tejinder P. Singh
We study an aligned direct-pairing construction of fermion masses from exceptional Jordan spectra. A coassociative restriction on an equal-diagonal Euclidean Albert element gives an equally spaced spectrum, while leaving its dimensionless spacing free. Restriction of the auxiliary symmetric cube to the monomial groups $Δ(3n^2)$ and $Δ(6n^2)$, for every $n\ge4$, classifies its invariant triplet selectors. Each triplet occurs once, but covariant mass operators retain substantial freedom beyond a fixed pairing. Our principal result is a complete joint quark test within this aligned class. Keeping a common spectral spacing and the centre ratio $s_u/s_d=2/3$, we allow every real spacing, all invariant triplets and independent positive hierarchy exponents in the two quark sectors. Logarithmic mass-shape ratios eliminate both exponents and reduce the down-sector constraint to seven inverse branches. Outward-rounded interval bounds show that every branch fails the up-sector test in the published marginal-input boxes at nine Standard Model benchmarks from the electroweak scale to $10^{16}\,\mathrm{GeV}$. The result also survives explicit padding for printed-number rounding. These boxes carry no joint confidence level and do not include model-dependent theoretical corrections. Earlier monomial prescriptions and one-parameter modular models provide complementary comparisons. The results constrain a specified mass law while leaving the broader Clifford-Jordan programme open. Reproducibility code is supplied.

♻ ☆ Lattice QCD determination of the $γZ$ box contribution to the proton weak charge
Zhao-long Zhang, Xu Feng, Mikhail Gorchtein, Lu-Chang Jin, Chuan Liu, Chien-Yeah Seng
We present the first lattice QCD determination of the $γZ$ box contribution to parity-violating electron-proton scattering, $\square_{γZ}$, a key ingredient for the precise tests of the Standard Model via the proton weak charge. Our calculation covers the electron beam energies up to $E=155$ MeV. At $E=0$, the vector contribution is known analytically and excluded by convention; for the remaining axial-vector component we obtain $\square_{γZ}(0)=0.00411(9)$. Incorporating this result implies a value for weak charge of $Q_W^p=0.06987(50)$. The calculated energy dependence of $\square_{γZ}$ is directly relevant to the upcoming P2 experiment at Mainz, which will operate at the optimized beam energy of 155 MeV to extract $Q_W^p$.Although the systematic error budget in this exploratory study is not yet complete, this work establishes a lattice-QCD framework for computing the $γZ$ box contribution and demonstrates the feasibility of a first-principles approach, providing a foundation for future calculations with improved systematic control.

♻ ☆ Testing Electromagnetic Memory and Aharonov--Bohm Effect via Acceleration-Imprinted Superconducting Phases
Jie Sheng, Tsutomu T. Yanagida, Bo Gao, Hong Ding
Electromagnetic memory is an infrared observable of gauge theory associated with soft photons and large gauge transformations. Despite its fundamental theoretical importance, it has not yet been experimentally verified. From a phenomenological perspective, a transient electromagnetic configuration can leave a persistent gauge-invariant phase imprint on charged coherent states after the local field has vanished through electric Aharonov-Bohm effect. We point out that the electric field and associated gauge potential induced inside a normal conductor by gravitational acceleration can imprint this phase without requiring external phase-imprinting electric field. It can then be read out through a superconducting protocol. For representative parameters, the predicted signal can lie within the range of present sensitivities, providing a possible tabletop route toward testing both electromagnetic memory and Aharonov-Bohm effect.

♻ ☆ Chiral Couplings of a Light Lmu-Ltau-like Z': Reinterpretation of CMS Four-Muon Data and High-Luminosity LHC Projections
Cesar Rendon
We reinterpret the CMS search for a light $Z^\prime$ boson in $Z\to4μ$ events with $77.3~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ at $\sqrt{s}=13$~TeV for a $Z^\prime$ with the flavor structure of $L_μ-L_τ$ and independent left- and right-handed couplings, parametrized by $ε=g_R/g_L$. Signal events are simulated with \textsc{MadGraph5\_aMC@NLO}, \textsc{Pythia}~8 and \textsc{Delphes} and analyzed with the event selection of the CMS search, while the background is digitized from the same CMS publication. For the vector model ($ε=1$) the expected limits agree with those of CMS within $9\%$ over $5$--$62$~GeV. For chiral couplings, $ε=-1,3,7,\infty$, we separate the effects on the production cross section, the branching ratio and the acceptance. For the axial model ($ε=-1$) the production cross section and the acceptance are the same as for the vector model. For $|g_L|\neq|g_R|$ the production cross section decreases by up to 15\% and the acceptance by up to 9\% at low masses, while the branching ratio increases. The expected limit on $\bar g=\sqrt{(g_L^2+g_R^2)/2}$ changes by at most $15\%$, and rescaling the vector limits with the ratio of branching ratios only overestimates the sensitivity by up to 12\%. For right-handed-dominated couplings, constraints from neutrino trident production, which require a coupling to neutrinos, no longer apply, while the four-muon channel remains sensitive through $g_R$. We project the sensitivity of the High-Luminosity LHC with $3000~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ at $\sqrt{s}=14$~TeV under several assumptions on the background systematic uncertainty and on pileup, reaching $\bar g\simeq1.5$--$2.1\times10^{-3}$ at $m_{Z^\prime}=5$~GeV.
comment: 13 pages, 7 figures
♻ ☆ Fractal phase structure of QCD under imaginary rotation
Rin Takada
We show that in hot QCD rotating at an imaginary angular velocity $\tildeΩ_I$, the angular velocity selects not only the temperature of the bulk but whether charge conjugation $C$ is broken there. For QCD at temperature $T$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $θ$, with $\tildeΩ_I/2π=p/q$ in lowest terms, the bulk far from the rotation axis is in the same thermal equilibrium state as nonrotating QCD at temperature $T/q$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $θ'=qθ+π(p+q+1)$; this follows from the Euclidean boundary conditions and locality alone, and holds nonperturbatively whenever the equivalent nonrotating system has a finite correlation length. Consequently, even at zero quark chemical potential, the bulk is placed at the Roberge-Weiss (RW) point whenever $p$ and $q$ are both odd, and $C$ is spontaneously broken there for $T>qT_{\rm RW}$, with $T_{\rm RW}$ the RW endpoint temperature. The bulks at $\tildeΩ_I=2π/3$ and $4π/3$, for example, are both at temperature $T/3$, yet only the former can break $C$. The set of imaginary angular velocities at which $C$ is broken has a fractal structure: raising $T$ adds rationals of ever larger denominator. At irrational $\tildeΩ_I/2π$ the bulk corresponds to zero-temperature QCD at any $T$ and remains confined.
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures
♻ ☆ Polarized Nuclear DVCS at the EIC
Jackson R. Pybus, Xuan Li, Liliet Calero-Diaz
The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will enable a series of measurements at unprecedented energies and luminosities, providing new opportunities to investigate the microscopic structure of nucleons and nuclei at small $x_B$. Exclusive processes such as Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering (DVCS) offer unique access to the three-dimensional structure of hadrons through Generalized Parton Distributions (GPDs), while polarized electron and ion beams further enable detailed studies of spin-dependent structure. A model for coherent DVCS on polarized $^3$Heis developed and applied to simulations of for $9\times166$-GeV $e^3$He collisions at the EIC. Using this framework, the statistical precision achievable is estimated for measurements of beam-spin asymmetries and for the extraction of the Compton Form Factors (CFFs) $\mathcal H_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ and $\tilde{\mathcal H}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$. Early EIC data are found to enable precise differential measurements of the unpolarized CFF $\mathcal H_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ and to provide significant constraints on its real and imaginary components. By contrast, meaningful constraints on the polarized CFF $\tilde{\mathcal H}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ require substantially larger integrated luminosities. The kinematics of the recoil $^3$He nucleus are also examined, and the advanced far-forward detector capabilities at the EIC required to tag the intact nucleus and perform fully exclusive measurements of coherent nuclear DVCS are discussed.
♻ ☆ Pretraining on boosted boson decays for polarization tagging of hadronic $W$ bosons
Saptaparna Bhattacharya
Longitudinally polarized weak bosons probe the unitarization of vector-boson scattering. At large boosts, longitudinal and transverse $W$ bosons produce jets with the same mass and two-prong structure, distinguished only by the decay angle. Longitudinal bosons are rare in $W$+jet events at these large boosts. We ask where the polarization information of a boosted $W$ boson lies and how much a tagger can recover. Requiring both decay quarks within the jet truncates the decay-angle distribution at an edge set by $m/(p_T R)$, which, as we show, bounds any hadronic polarization tagger. Within this acceptance, the decay angle carries nearly all the polarization information of a jet in $W$+jet events. Whether pretraining retains the decay angle is not obvious, so we pretrain a point-edge transformer on $10^7$ unpolarized boosted-boson, top-quark and QCD jets and fine-tune it with $10^3$ to $5\times10^4$ labeled jets per class. With the fewest labels, a boosted decision tree on substructure observables performs best; with the most labels, the strongest networks come within 0.003 in AUC of the ideal decay-angle tagger. Pretraining saves a factor of about two to three in labels, and our boson pretraining improves on a generic one by a few thousandths in AUC, more with frozen transformer blocks. Student networks with a few hundred times fewer parameters, distilled with unlabeled jets, match their teacher. More information lies outside the jet. The production angle, reconstructed with the recoiling jet, improves every tagger. Complete transmission from a lower-level WZW model then imposes a lower bound on the coset central charge on the other side. In linear response, the relation fixes the ratio of thermal to charge conductance to the harmonic mean of the two bulk ratios, independently of the interface, while coset sectors bound the thermal conductance at fixed charge conductance. This interface-independent ratio is a generalized Wiedemann--Franz law for conformal interfaces between WZW models. The charge transmission coefficient $k_{LR}$ also governs equilibrium charge fluctuations and fixes the leading quadratic dependence of the boundary-condition-changing operator's scaling dimension on the rotation angle.

We give a historical account on the growth of the field of ``AI-assisted mathematics'' in the last decade, and comment on what culminated in 2026 as perhaps the most dramatic year in the history of mathematics since Euclid.

In this work, we introduce the first scotogenic model based on a gauged $L_μ + L_τ$ symmetry whose spontaneous breaking by two units leaves a remnant matter parity $M_P$. The resulting light active neutrinos are of Majorana nature and the lightest electrically neutral state mediating the scotogenic loop is stabilized by $M_P$ and can be identified as a weakly interacting massive particle dark matter candidate. We analyze the phenomenology of a predominantly singlet-like CP-even scalar dark matter candidate and the representative regions of parameter space compatible with the observed thermal relic abundance. The $Z'$ boson is compatible with a broad range of parameters relevant for dark matter. In particular, electroweak precision constraints do not lead to significant tensions for kinetic mixing values up to $ε\sim 10^{-2}$. We discuss the implications of existing searches for leptophilic gauge bosons and the conditions under which visible and invisible collider signatures become relevant.

We prove that the renormalisation group flow of multiscalar $φ^4$ theory in four dimensions is a gradient flow to all orders in perturbation theory. The proof uses the Weyl consistency conditions of Osborn and Jack, and it assumes two properties of perturbation theory: that the generating functional with local couplings is finite (also assumed by Osborn and Jack), and that the known expansion of massive Feynman integrals at large momenta holds with a bound on its remainder at each momentum. The consistency conditions give a gradient formula in which the tensor that multiplies the beta function is allowed to have an antisymmetric part, determined by coefficients of the Weyl anomaly. We derive a Ward identity for the two-point function of the marginal operators at constant couplings away from fixed points, with sources for the currents of field rotations and for the mass operator. It re-expresses one of the anti-symmetric contributions in terms of two-point functions and the first moment of the three-point function. We show that, after this rewrite, each of the resulting terms is equivalent to a symmetric contribution to the metric and a contribution to the potential, and we give both explicitly. The metric is positive definite to all orders in perturbation theory. The proof implies in particular the four relations among five- and six-loop coefficients of the field rotation, which Pannell and Stergiou derived as the conditions for a gradient flow at six loops. We check by explicit computation that these relations indeed hold. A companion paper treats $d=4-\varepsilon$ and other critical dimensions with a Ward identity on the sphere.

We show that wormholes connecting multiple asymptotic boundaries always spontaneously break at least some of the symmetries preserved by their boundary conditions. Their configurations then form nontrivial orbits of the broken symmetry, and for the case of a fermionic symmetry, the contribution of each orbit vanishes. We conclude that wormholes do not contribute to moments of supersymmetric partition functions. This extends results on supersymmetric indices by Iliesiu, Kologlu, and Turiaci. We emphasize that supersymmetric partition functions can still have a nonzero ensemble variance. In SYK-like examples that we analyze, this arises due to the contribution of ``non-geometric wormhole'' configurations that preserve all continuous symmetries.

Unlike vacuum BPST instantons, these sourced instantons do not give rise to exponentially suppressed rates. We relate the winding number to the number of fermionic zero modes, suggesting an underlying index theorem for sourced instantons. We also calculate the closed-form expression for the leading-order correlator for fermion insertions both outside and inside the monopole core. Our results indicate that Rubakov-Callan catalysis is an IR effect where the scattering fermions do not reach the monopole core.

The obstruction is an antisymmetric contribution to the metric on the space of couplings, which has resisted removal since the work of Jack and Osborn more than 35 years ago. We show that a conformal Ward identity on the sphere allows it to be removed by a choice of scheme. The beta function is then the gradient of a potential $A$ with respect to a symmetric metric, to all orders in perturbation theory. The Ward identity gives this result in any dimension $d$, in theories with and without a Weyl anomaly. At leading order the metric is fixed by the two-point functions of the perturbing operators, so unitarity makes it positive definite at weak coupling. At fixed points $A$ equals $\widetilde{F}=\sin\tfrac{πd}{2}\,\ln Z_{S^{d}}$, so the $\widetilde{F}$-theorem follows for perturbative flows to all loop orders. We show that sources of relevant operators, which on the sphere mix with the curvature, do not affect these results. In unitary theories the only exception is the source of a free scalar field near $d=6,10,\ldots\,$, so that for $φ^3$ theory near six dimensions the gradient property remains open.

At fixed $ω$, with $ω_{\rm sp}\llω\ll e^{S_0/3}ω_{\rm sp}$ the Schwarzian growth then saturates at $η_{\max}\simeq0.174\,(ω/ω_{\rm sp})\,η_{sc}$, where $η_{sc}$ is the semiclassical viscosity, and the viscosity decreases at lower temperatures. At the extremely low temperature scale $CT\sim e^{-2S_0/3}$ the genus expansion and the one-loop entropy computations completely break down. There we start probing the edge of the spectrum and the problem reduces exactly to the Airy kernel. We find that the ratio of the quenched averages of $η$ and $s$ is finite and positive at every non-zero temperature. We compare our results with explicit completions defined by the string equation, in which the spectrum is bounded from below. The bulk results are the same in these completions and the quenched edge results change only by a few per cent, while the annealed quantities depend on the non-perturbative completion at order one.

♻ ☆ Estimation of covariance matrix for Stokes-like measurement under phase-space deformation

We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $θ$ and $η$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response. By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. We then formulate an interferometric detection scheme through Stokes-like measurements, in which the outgoing optical field is combined with a phase-controlled reference beam at a balanced beam splitter, and the resulting photocurrents are measured using photodetectors. The optical response provides access to the modified normal-mode frequencies, which enables us to estimate experimental values of $θ$ and $η$. Our results establish a theoretical connection between NC-space dynamics, Gaussian-state correlations, and experimentally accessible optical observables, suggesting an optomechanical route toward testing signatures of phase-space noncommutativity.
♻ ☆ Dynamical tidal response of neutron stars: From effective field theory to gravitational waveforms

We investigate the fully relativistic dynamical tidal response of neutron stars up to second order in the frequency. Combining the worldline effective field theory for extended gravitating bodies with perturbation theory of relativistic stellar models, we derive the tidal deformation induced by an external time-dependent field, including a universal logarithmic running term. In the effective theory, we work in dimensional regularization and, through a consistent matching procedure, obtain for the first time the complete leading-order dynamical tidal corrections to both the conservative dynamics and the gravitational-wave signal of compact binaries, including the scheme-dependent finite terms in addition to the running. We show that, in the relativistic regime, dynamical effects cannot be fully captured by mode excitations alone. The magnitude of the additional contribution depends on the stellar compactness, the equation of state, and the running term. Dynamical Love numbers are significantly enhanced with respect to their static counterparts for relatively small compactness. As a result, although they formally enter the gravitational-wave phase at eighth post-Newtonian order, dynamical tidal effects yield a nonnegligible contribution during the late inspiral. Using a Fisher-matrix analysis, we show that third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope could measure dynamical Love numbers for a range of neutron-star masses and equations of state. Conversely, neglecting these effects can lead to significant biases in the inference of static Love numbers, and hence on the nuclear equation of state. Our results highlight the importance of dynamical tidal effects for high-precision gravitational-wave modeling with future detectors.

The TEE is the pseudo entropy of a timelike interval. In the bulk, the imaginary part of the TEE comes from a timelike geodesic. After a Rindler transformation to a rotating BTZ black hole, the two spacelike extremal curves lie on the inner and outer horizons, and exchanging $l_u\leftrightarrow \ell l_φ$ takes one to the other. We clarify the geometric role of the timelike extremal curve in the Rindler frame. We show that it is the line $\tilde U=\tilde V=0$ stretched between the two horizons, starting on the inner horizon, touching the outer horizon at its midpoint, and returning to the inner one. No such curve exists outside the region between the horizons. Its length, $iπ\ell$, is independent of the interval, and it alone produces the imaginary part $iπc/6$. We follow the same procedure in flat space holography, where the spacelike curve sits on the cosmological horizon and the timelike curve lies between the cosmological horizon and timelike infinity. Evaluating the holographic TEE for a timelike interval in CCFT$_2$ on the plane, we find that, in contrast with the cylinder, the real and imaginary parts are equal.

♻ ☆ Cosmological Collider in the Grassmannian
Mattia Arundine, Guilherme L. Pimentel
We revisit the computation of four-point wavefunction coefficients and correlators for external conformally coupled scalars exchanging a particle of generic mass and spin. Much of the phenomenology of cosmological collider physics in the near-de Sitter limit follows from these functions. Computing them in detail is a central challenge in the cosmological bootstrap. Using the cosmological Grassmannian, we write these objects in closed form using hypergeometric functions and Legendre polynomials. We achieve this by writing the standard bootstrap differential equation using the Plücker coordinates of the Grassmannian, and using the basis of Mandelstam invariants. The exchange in the s-channel can be written in terms of a hypergeometric function of the S Mandelstam, while the spin information appears as an overall Legendre polynomial factor that also depends on the other Mandelstams. We fix the boundary conditions by first demanding the absence of unphysical singularities, and, for correlators, by further matching to a kinematic limit in momentum space. Our formulae in Grassmannian space are much simpler than their counterparts in momentum space, demonstrating another useful application of the Grassmannian as a kinematic space for cosmology.

We construct modular flows associated with spacelike and timelike intervals in AdS$_{3}$/CFT$_{2}$ and extend this framework to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$. Beginning with the boundary symmetry generators, we explicitly derive the boundary modular flows and extend them into the bulk, providing a systematic procedure that relates bulk modular flows to the extremal curves and holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. For spacelike intervals, the resulting bulk modular flows determine the extremal curves, whose integrated line elements reproduce the standard holographic entanglement entropy. We then generalize this approach to timelike intervals, explicitly constructing the modular flows whose fixed points reproduce the extremal spacelike and timelike curves, which give the holographic timelike entanglement entropy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first explicit construction of the modular flow associated with a timelike extremal curve for a timelike interval. The same procedure is then carried over to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$, which gives rise to the holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. Finally, we show that the flat space results obtained in this work can be recovered from their AdS$_3$ counterparts in the flat space limit.

When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory form a statistical manifold, whose Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions. For the two-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions in the large-$N$ limit, we study the continuum limit, in which the lattice spacing $a$ goes to zero at fixed mass gap $Λ$, through the Fisher metric of the distribution of the auxiliary field $σ$. The renormalization condition fixes an expectation coordinate, and dimensional transmutation becomes an exponential relation between it and a natural coordinate. The main result is that the $a\to0$ limits differ between the Fisher metric of the long-distance modes, whose momenta are fixed in physical units, and that of the full $P(σ)$. In the former, the infinitely many irrelevant directions that change the kinetic term locally shrink relative to the mass-term direction to order $aΛ\log(1/(aΛ))$ or smaller, and several modes together leave only the two directions $(Λ,m)$ of the continuum theory. In the latter, the kinetic-term directions shrink as fast as the mass-term direction, and the difference in the regularization remains in lattice-scale correlations. In the eight-dimensional space of local deformations examined numerically, the one exception is the deformation that only adds a contact term to the propagator, which as $a\to0$ becomes indistinguishable from a change of $1/g^2$ in both metrics. In the Fisher metric of the full $P(σ)$, the curvature of the coupling plane at fixed kinetic term diverges as $(1/2)\log^2(1/(aΛ))$, not as the correlation volume often assumed in thermodynamic geometry, and the critical point lies at infinite distance in this plane.

We investigate the asymptotic behavior of Kaluza-Klein (KK) towers in warped compactifications to Minkowski space. Focusing on the overall decompactification limit, we derive the scaling of KK masses at large KK momentum for scalar fluctuations in lower-dimensional Planck units. In codimension-one warped backgrounds sourced by a higher-dimensional exponential potential, we solve explicitly for the internal profiles and obtain a closed expression for the exponential mass decay rate $λ_{\rm KK}$ of the tower in terms of the moduli space distance. We find that warping reduces $λ_{\rm KK}$ relative to the unwarped case, in such a way that sufficiently strong warping could in principle violate the Sharpened Distance Conjecture bound. Remarkably, this sharpened bound is still satisfied precisely when the higher-dimensional potential obeys the condition forbidding asymptotic accelerated expansion, establishing a direct link between the Sharpened Distance Conjecture and the Strong de Sitter condition in one higher dimension. We also argue that for higher-codimension warped backgrounds the asymptotic KK scaling remains unmodified.

These methods cover both the real-time and imaginary-time formalisms. By analyzing all interactions in detail, it is shown that, in perturbation theory, only the propagators are affected by the average angular momentum and the chemical potentials, the vertices remain unmodified. Euler regularized the divergent product of all positive integers and found beautiful formulas for regularized sums of integer powers of positive integers. These derivations essentially relied on what is now called the zeta-regularization technique, although analytical continuation had not yet been invented. This classic method is however not applicable to the product of all primes, as the prime zeta function has a natural boundary along the imaginary axis. Muñoz García and Pérez-Marco overcame this obstacle and evaluated the product of all primes to $4π^2$ by finding an appropriately regularized value of the derivative of the prime zeta function at the origin, lying on the natural boundary. Their approach heavily relies on the Möbius function and could therefore be called a Möbius regularization. We extend this approach in two novel directions. First, we show how to make sense of the sum of all primes. This regularization requires going a finite distance beyond the natural boundary. Second, we determine the regularized products of integers and primes in the nine imaginary quadratic fields where integers have a unique factorization into primes, and establish a general power-law relationship between products of integers and primes. Two well-known examples are Gauss and Eisenstein integers. The interest in this approach goes beyond number theory. In a variety of physical situations, the zeta-regularization technique is indeed not applicable because the relevant zeta function has a natural boundary.

The standard "no-go theorem" against late-time solutions to the Hubble tension is essentially a normalization wall, since Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) measurements constrain the product $H_0r_d$, with $r_d$ the sound horizon at baryon drag. However, late-time solutions (which keep $r_d$ fixed) are tightly constrained not only by the BAO normalization $H_0r_d$, but also by the shape of the expansion history, i.e. the dimensionless expansion rate $E(z) \equiv H(z)/H_0$. We show that, if $r_d$ and the acoustic angular scale $θ_s$ are fixed, an increase in $H_0$ needs to be matched by an equal fractional increase in the dimensionless distance integral $I \equiv \int dz/E(z)$: $δH_0/H_0 \simeq δI/I$. We use this to quantify the "shape wall" set by relative distance constraints on $E(z)$, which we reconstruct nonparametrically, using Gaussian Processes and the latest unanchored Type Ia Supernovae (SNeIa) and BAO data. In our most conservative analysis using PantheonPlus SNeIa and DESI DR2 BAO data, we find a maximum fractional increase in $H_0$ of $\lesssim 2\%$, falling well short of the $\gtrsim 8\%$ required to solve the tension. This shape wall holds even in the presence of early-time new physics, and limits the maximum increase in $H_0$ which can be contributed by late-time modifications to $E(z)$ at fixed $θ_s$. Therefore, late-time modifications, whether invoked alone or alongside early-time new physics, face not only the well-known normalization wall, but also a stringent percent-level shape wall.

We systematically develop a framework for equilibrium thermodynamics in terms of thermodynamic representations, which are choices of thermodynamic potential and independent variables, one from each conjugate pair. In each representation, equations of state arise from first derivatives of the potential and response functions from its second derivatives. We apply this framework to ideal gases and to Schwarzschild black holes in a spherical cavity in various representations, interpreting the cavity area and its conjugate surface pressure as the thermodynamic volume and pressure of a holographically dual system. For this quasi-local Schwarzschild black hole, stability depends on the thermodynamic representation, or equivalently on which variables are held fixed under equilibrium perturbations. The large black hole branch is thermally stable at fixed volume but mechanically unstable under isothermal compression, while the system is mechanically stable under adiabatic compression everywhere. At fixed pressure, the black hole is thermally unstable throughout the physical state space. We also find that the thermal expansion coefficient is negative everywhere and show that isenthalpic expansion always cools the black hole. More broadly, the framework provides a systematic route to deriving equations of state and response functions for a wide class of black hole systems using quasi-local gravitational thermodynamics.

At subleading order, the gravitational field is determined by three additional sets of charges: the super-Lorentz charges, the leading mixed tail/ peeling-breaking charges and the leading peeling-breaking charges. In this work we provide a proper-supertranslation-invariant definition of these charges in terms of asymptotic Bondi-Sachs fields as well as a corresponding proper supertranslation and logarithmic translation invariant definition of these charges in terms of Beig-Schmidt fields. Using the properties of homogeneous and inhomogeneous solutions to relevant wave equations over the boundary de Sitter spacetime at spatial infinity, we derive the conservation law of super-Lorentz charges between the future and past of spatial infinity. We obtain that the super-Lorentz aspects are non-locally defined from the Bondi-Sachs fields.

We define this free radiation as the out-state, extracted from the light-cone residue of the kernel for each scalar pair via a classical LSZ-type reduction formula. ♻ ☆ Probing Topological Phases in a Strongly Correlated Ladder Model via Entanglement

This work examines the interplay of band topology and interactions in a spinless two-leg ladder with $p$-wave-like inter-orbital hybridization. In the non-interacting limit, the model hosts three topologically distinct insulating phases, denoted by $A$, $B$, and $C$. Combining density-matrix renormalization group calculations with low-energy theories of the critical lines yields the interacting phase diagram for an inter-orbital density-density interaction. The $A$-$C$ boundary contains two Dirac valleys and has central charge $c=2$ in the free theory. In the presence of interaction, the exact reflection symmetry pins the $A$-$C$ boundary to its free-theory location, while the critical theory evolves to $c=1$ and the edge entanglement entropy changes from $2\ln 2$ to $\ln 2$. The $B$-$C$ boundary contains a single Dirac mode and shifts quadratically with interaction strength through second-order self-energy corrections involving virtual heavy modes, while retaining its $c=1$ critical structure. Charge conservation and antiunitary many-body chiral symmetry give an interacting $\mathbb{Z}_4$ classification. This distinguishes the two interacting topological phases despite their identical lowest entanglement-spectrum degeneracy. The boundary response is governed by the symmetry and operator content of its critical theory and the symmetry-protected topology of the adjoining phases.

♻ ☆ From Self-Dual to Physical $\mathbb{C}P^{N-1}$: Anomalies, Boundary Stokes Phenomenon, and Global Structure of $θ$-vacua

We introduce a two-coupling generalization of $\mathbb{C}P^{N-1}$ model that continuously interpolates between the self-dual ($ε=0$) and the physical ($ε=g$) theories as a useful nonperturbative tool. At $ε\neq g$, this model possesses a chiral imbalance, which may be viewed as a real topological deformation (imaginary-$θ$). We demonstrate that exact quantum equivalence between first- and second-order formulations strictly requires a topological counterterm sourced by a bosonic chiral anomaly. Solving this deformed theory at large $N$ yields two primary results. First, we analytically determine the nonperturbative vacuum structure of the self-dual theory, a self-dual vacuum with a dynamically generated field-strength condensate. Second, we resolve a fundamental paradox where saddles with $(θ+ 2πn) \sim O(N)$ ($n$ is branch number) spuriously yield lower energy densities than the physical ground state. Because the effective action possesses an essential singularity at $F=0$, we show that the Lefschetz thimble analysis must be generalized to include boundary thimbles. A boundary Stokes phenomenon renders the problematic saddles topologically inactive, fully restoring the validity of the large-$N$ expansion for strongly coupled theories.

♻ ☆ Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
Fedor K. Popov, Leonardo Rastelli
We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^\natural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^\natural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^\natural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups. A separate package in the repository imports that library's generation theorem for the model and proves, with no hypotheses, that $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^\natural$ is isomorphic to the model, compatibly with the Griess algebras, and that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. It also formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own. This note announces release v1.1, which moves the whole library to Lean v4.35.

♻ ☆ Casimir effect in Gribov-Zwanziger theory
David Dudal, Philipe De Fabritiis, Sebbe Stouten, David Vercauteren
We consider Yang-Mills theory with two infinite parallel plates, separated by a distance \(L\), that are perfect magnetic conductors (PMC) or perfect electric conductors (PEC). Recently, it was shown that the Gribov copy problem persists in such a setting. We then study the Gribov-Zwanziger (GZ) action in the presence of those boundaries using functional integral methods. Lagrange multiplier fields allow one to lift the boundary conditions into the action, after which the boundary modifications to the gluon propagator can straightforwardly be determined. In the PEC case, we provide evidence that, even when translation invariance is (partially) broken, the usual horizon term in the GZ action still restricts the functional integral to the Gribov region. We compute the Casimir energy for GZ with PMC or PEC plates, both directly from the functional integral and from the energy-momentum tensor, obtaining consistent results. We compare our analytical results with recent lattice data, in both 4D and 3D. A priori, one might expect that the boundary-modified gluon propagator introduces new \(L\)-dependencies into the GZ gap equation. This would make the Gribov mass \(γ\) dynamically dependent on \(L\), implying an interesting interplay with the Casimir energy. However, we show that no such dynamical \(L\)-dependence occurs within the current approximation.

♻ ☆ Quasi-local form for $α$--$z$ Rényi QNEC from fixed-ray escorts
Tanay Kibe, Pratik Roy
Rényi divergences generalize relative entropy and measure the distinguishability of quantum states, but their relation to energy and entanglement entropy is less direct than for ordinary relative entropy. We introduce and study an energy--entropy relation for Rényi divergences by making use of an integral representation that expresses the $α$--$z$ Rényi divergence as an average of ordinary relative entropies of auxiliary escort states constructed from the excited state and the reference state. The integral representation gives energy--entropy decompositions, averaged entanglement laws and energy bounds in regulated quantum field theory (QFT). We further obtain a quasi-local expression for the diagonal second null shape variation of the $α$--$z$ Rényi divergence of an excited state relative to the QFT vacuum. This expression contains a transport term because forming an escort after restricting to a smaller region generally differs from restricting an escort formed beforehand. The conjectural $α$--$z$ Rényi quantum null energy condition (QNEC) then gives a lower bound on the null energy density of the average escort state. As in the ordinary QNEC, the bound involves a second null variation of von Neumann entropy, here averaged over the escort ensemble. We verify the conjecture for an exactly solvable family of coherent excitations of a free scalar field throughout the finite-divergence part of the upper data-processing region. For this family, the sandwiched Rényi divergence at fixed $α>1$ has a positive diagonal second null shape variation that is entirely accounted for by the transport term. We also show that escort formation commutes with the reduced encoding channel in finite-dimensional operator-algebra quantum error-correcting codes with exact complementary recovery.

♻ ☆ Fractionalized Fermi liquids and the cuprate phase diagram
Pietro M. Bonetti, Maine Christos, Alexander Nikolaenko, Aavishkar A. Patel, Subir Sachdev
We review a theoretical framework for the cuprate superconductors, rooted in a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*) description of the intermediate-temperature pseudogap phase at low doping. The FL* theory predicted hole pockets each of fractional area $p/8$ at hole doping $p$, in contrast to the area $p/4$ in spin density wave theory. Magnetotransport measurements, including observation of the Yamaji angle, show clear evidence of hole pocket quasiparticles which can tunnel coherently between square lattice layers, and are consistent with the FL* description. The FL* phase of a single-band model is described using a layer construction with a pair of ancilla qubits on each site: the Ancilla Layer Model (ALM). Fluctuations are described by the SU(2) gauge theory of a background spin liquid with critical Dirac spinons. A Monte Carlo study of the thermal SU(2) gauge theory transforms the hole pockets into Fermi arcs in photoemission. One route to confinement of FL* upon lowering temperature yields a $d$-wave superconductor via a Kosterlitz-Thouless transition of $h/(2e)$ vortices, with nodal Bogoliubov quasiparticles featuring anisotropic velocities and vortices surrounded by charge order halos. Increasing doping from the FL* phase in the ALM drives a transition to a conventional Fermi liquid (FL) at large doping, passing through an intermediate strange metal regime. We formulate a theory of the FL*-FL metal-metal transition without a symmetry-breaking order parameter, using a critical quantum `charge' liquid of mobile electrons in the presence of disorder, developed via an extension of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model to two spatial dimensions. At low temperatures, and across optimal and over doping, we address the regimes of extended non-Fermi liquid behavior by Griffiths effects near quantum phase transitions in disordered metals.

♻ ☆ Constraints on the volume enclosed by Fermi surfaces
Subir Sachdev
A fundamental property of a Fermi liquid (FL) is that the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by $ρ$, the total density of electrons. In a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*), the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by the same expression after $ρ$ has been shifted by a quantized amount, most commonly to $ρ-1$ (we assume spin rotation invariance, for simplicity). The FL* shift is related to the quantized symmetry fractionalization data of a quantum spin liquid, whose fractionalized spinon excitations are present alongside the Fermi surface quasiparticles. In this review article, we establish the FL* Fermi volume by generalizing the original Luttinger proof for FL to parton gauge theories of the quantum spin liquid and FL*. We also discuss Oshikawa's flux insertion arguments for FL, and their extension to FL*, including a discussion of gapless spin liquids.

♻ ☆ On the Casimir effect with mixed dynamical edge mode and perfect electromagnetic conducting boundary conditions
Jarne Devroe, David Dudal, Sebbe Stouten
We study the Casimir effect for a parallel plate setup with one plate with dynamical edge mode (DEM) boundary conditions, and one plate with perfect electromagnetic conductor (PEMC) boundary conditions. In order to restore BRST invariance, new edge fields are introduced on the DEM plate. We then lift the boundary conditions into the action using Lagrange multiplier fields, and integrate out the bulk fields to obtain a non-local effective boundary theory from which we compute the Casimir energy. The resulting Casimir force is identical to a PMC-PEMC setup, implying that, from the point of view of the Casimir effect, a DEM plate is equivalent to a PMC plate. We also include a detailed derivation of the general functional method used to compute the Casimir energy from the partition function.

We adapt Henyey's construction, although the boundary configuration imposes extra restrictions on the ansatz for the gauge field. Second, we discuss the phenomenon of an emergent boundary gauge invariance for PEC and PMC plates in Yang-Mills theory. This shall be important when applying the Gribov-Zwanziger procedure to parallel plate setups, of relevance for non-perturbatively studying the non-Abelian Casimir effect in the future.

♻ ☆ Quantum Metric and Nonlinear Hall Effect of Photons
Keidai Akiba, Naoki Yamamoto
Using the path-integral formalism, we show that photons possess a nontrivial quantum metric in momentum space. We derive the semiclassical action and equations of motion by taking into account the quantum metric. In media with a spatially varying refractive index $n(\mathbf{x})$, the quantum metric induces a shift in the trajectory of light at second order in spatial gradients of $n$, whose transverse component may be regarded as a nonlinear Hall effect of light. The quantum metric also gives rise to corrections to photon propagation relevant to gravitational lensing in curved spacetime at second order in wavelength, including a gravitational nonlinear Hall effect arising from the interplay between the geometry of position space and that of momentum space.
