Motivated by recent THz pump-probe experiments in unconventional superconductors, in this paper we use Keldysh--Nambu quasiclassical theory of $d$-wave superconductors to analyze the third-harmonic generation. A systematic perturbative solution of the out-of-equilibrium Eilenberger equation for the Keldysh propagator is developed with respect to the amplitude of an external electromagnetic field. We show that in a clean superconductor and for a spatially uniform electromagnetic field third harmonic response is absent. In the presence of elastic impurity scattering which we treat using the self-consistent scattering matrix approximation in the Born limit we find that the third-harmonic current density is a sum of the Higgs (amplitude) mode and quasiparticle contributions. We compute their dependence on disorder, temperature, frequency and polarization of external radiation.
comment: 20 pages, 5 figures, 58 references
♻ ☆ Two Unconventional Hall Effects in the Kagome Magnet TmMn4Cr$_2$Sn$_6$
Mohamed El Gazzah, Fehmi Sami Yasin, Bishal Thapa, Sk Jamaluddin, Daniel Lu, Abhijeet Nayak, Resham Babu Regmi, Mary Katherine Carroll, Igor I. Mazin, Nirmal J. Ghimire
We identify two Hall anomalies in the kagome magnet TmMn$_4$Cr$_2$Sn$_6$. We propose that the high-field anomaly reflects a discontinuous spin reorientation and differing sublattice contributions to Hall transport and magnetization. At low fields, Hall hysteresis persists despite negligible magnetic hysteresis, suggesting a chirality-related contribution, although its microscopic origin remains unresolved. These contrasting regimes show how magnetic transitions can mimic unconventional Hall signals and highlight the limits of magnetization-based Hall decomposition.
♻ ☆ Dynamics and stability of U(1) spin liquids beyond mean-field theory: Triangular-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model
Josef Willsher, Johannes Knolle
Quantum spin liquids (QSLs) are long-range entangled phases of frustrated magnets exhibiting fractionalised spin excitations. In two dimensions, there is limited analytical understanding of their excitation spectra beyond parton mean-field theories, which fail to capture many features of the finite frequency dynamical response. We use a self-consistent mean-field theory combined with the random phase approximation (RPA) for the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model on the triangular lattice to describe the strong spinon-spinon interactions of the U(1) Dirac QSL. We obtain quantitative results for the dynamical spin structure factor and phase diagram compatible with comprehensive numerical efforts. We show the continuum response at the Brillouin zone corners is described by a spinon-exciton hybridised with monopole gauge excitations. We further show that the transition from the QSL to 120-degree coplanar order is in the QED$_3$ O(3)-GN universality class. We extend the method to chiral QSLs and XXZ anisotropy, and discuss its broad range of applicability to other models and for describing inelastic neutron scattering experiments in KYbSe$_2$.
comment: 17 pages; 8 figures
♻ ☆ Efficient Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Long-time Quantum Dynamics
Marko Maležič, Johann Ostmeyer
Accurately simulating long-time dynamics of many-body systems is a challenge in both classical and quantum computing due to the accumulation of Trotter errors. While low-order Trotter-Suzuki decompositions are straightforward to implement, their rapidly growing error limits access to long-time observables. We present a framework for constructing efficient high-order Trotter-Suzuki schemes by identifying their structure and directly optimizing their parameters over a high-dimensional space. This method enables the discovery of new schemes with significantly improved efficiency compared to traditional constructions, such as those by Suzuki and Yoshida. Based on the theoretical efficiency and practical performance, we recommend two novel highly efficient schemes at $4^{\textrm{th}}$ and $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of these decompositions on the Heisenberg model and the quantum harmonic oscillator, and find that for a fixed final time they perform better across the computational cost. Even when using large time steps, they surpass established low-order schemes like the Leapfrog. Finally, we investigate the in-practice performance of different Trotter schemes and find the decompositions with more uniform coefficients tend to feature improved error accumulation over long times. We have included this observation into our choice of recommended schemes.
comment: 28 + 7 pages, 11 figures, 5 tables and 1 animation; v2 (published version): Added scheme comparison table and fixed grouping mistake, v3: fixed origin point typo, v4: fixed mistake in Eq.(27)
♻ ☆ Probing Topological Phases in a Strongly Correlated Ladder Model via Entanglement
Aminul Hussain, Nisa Ara, Rudranil Basu, Sudeshna Sen
This work examines the interplay of band topology and interactions in a spinless two-leg ladder with $p$-wave-like inter-orbital hybridization. In the non-interacting limit, the model hosts three topologically distinct insulating phases, denoted by $A$, $B$, and $C$. Combining density-matrix renormalization group calculations with low-energy theories of the critical lines yields the interacting phase diagram for an inter-orbital density-density interaction. The $A$-$C$ boundary contains two Dirac valleys and has central charge $c=2$ in the free theory. In the presence of interaction, the exact reflection symmetry pins the $A$-$C$ boundary to its free-theory location, while the critical theory evolves to $c=1$ and the edge entanglement entropy changes from $2\ln 2$ to $\ln 2$. The $B$-$C$ boundary contains a single Dirac mode and shifts quadratically with interaction strength through second-order self-energy corrections involving virtual heavy modes, while retaining its $c=1$ critical structure. Charge conservation and antiunitary many-body chiral symmetry give an interacting $\mathbb{Z}_4$ classification. This distinguishes the two interacting topological phases despite their identical lowest entanglement-spectrum degeneracy. The boundary response is governed by the symmetry and operator content of its critical theory and the symmetry-protected topology of the adjoining phases.
comment: Analytical calculations and explanations are added. (23 pages, 14 figures, 7 appendices)
♻ ☆ Electronic structure, quasiparticle renormalizations, and magnetic correlations in the alternating single-layer bilayer nickelate La$_5$Ni$_3$O$_{11}$
I. V. Leonov
Using DFT+DMFT we study the electronic structure and magnetic correlations in the recently discovered alternating single-layer bilayer Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate La$_5$Ni$_3$O$_{11}$ (1212-LNO). Our results exhibit qualitative differences for the structurally distinct single-layer and bilayer Ni ions, implying the importance of confinement and orbital-dependent correlations. The Ni $e_g$ states originating from the bilayer Ni ions form strongly renormalized quasiparticle bands with a large enhancement factor $m^*/m \sim 3.5$ and 4.2 for the Ni $x^2-y^2$ and $3z^2-r^2$ orbitals. Moreover, the $e_g$ states of the single-layer Ni ions exhibit an orbital-selective Mott insulating state, with a narrow energy gap for the Ni $3z^2-r^2$ states and metallic, strongly non-Fermi-liquid Ni $x^2-y^2$ ones. Our analysis of magnetic correlations suggests the formation of intertwined spin and charge density wave stripes in the bilayer NiO$_6$ slab, in close similarity to the double-layer material. We identify two major instabilities: a leading one associated with a propagating wave vector ${\bf Q}=(\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3})$ ("up-down-0" spin pattern or "$d^8$-$d^8$-$d^8\underline{L}$'' charge-density wave with Ni $d^8\underline{L}$ ions bonded in an interlayer spin polaron), competing with $(\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{4})$ ("up-up-down-down") stripe state. The single-layer Ni $3d$ electrons exhibit an instability toward the Néel magnetic state. Under pressure, 1212-LNO undergoes an orbital-selective Mott insulator-to-metal transition, associated with metallization of the single-layer Ni $e_g$ states. The single-layer Ni $e_g$ bands exhibit non-Fermi-liquid behavior with strongly incoherent spectral weights near $E_F$. We note that correlation effects result in a crossover from single-layer (as obtained within DFT) to double-layer dominated magnetic correlations.

♻ ☆ Spectral Moments of the Projected Hubbard Configuration Graph: Connectivity, Exchange, and Virtual Doublons
D. Souza
At strong repulsion, the lowest band of $n$ lattice fermions is the spectrum of the hopping projected onto states without double occupancy, $H_\infty=P_0H_tP_0$. We study its moments on the square lattice and, where possible, any finite graph. (1) For spin-independent Hermitian hopping (no on-site terms) on $N\geq2$ sites, $μ_2=\frac{n(N-n)}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}|t_{ij}|^2$ for any spin composition. (2) On any finite graph, $μ_4$ is exactly linear in the same-spin pair count $P_{\rm same}$ (four hops move at most three particles). For uniform hopping on a simple graph with $N\geq4$, $μ_4=A+αP_{\rm same}$ in closed form: the slope $α=-8C_4(N-n)(8N-11n-2)/[N(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)]$ is set by the number $C_4$ of 4-cycles, the intercept, via hard-core bosons, by edge, edge-pair and 4-cycle counts. With arbitrary Peierls phases, $μ_4$ is a spin-independent baseline plus a coefficient times $\sum_C\cosΘ_C$ over 4-cycle Wilson phases. (3) At finite $U$, the second-order Schrieffer-Wolff correction is Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal to $H_\infty$ on every triangle-free graph, so the band variance has no $1/U$ term; its $U^{-2}$ coefficient is negative at the low fillings computed. (4) Exchange loops carry the ordinary charge-$e$ harmonic, $α\cosΦ_\square$ on $L\times L$ tori, $L\neq4$, while the doublon hopping acquires a doubled phase, $t_de^{2iA_{ij}}$: the second-order single-doublon Hamiltonian is exactly $π$-periodic ($h/2e$) under a boundary twist, and the exact two-electron U-band follows up to $O((2λ)^L/U^{L-1})$. Result (1), the closed form in (2) without phases, the orthogonality in (3) and the doubled phase are machine-checked in Lean 4. Repulsive binding and the pair charge $2e$ are known; new are the exact moments and the derivation of the doubled phase. We make no claim about many-pair phase stiffness, off-diagonal long-range order or superconductivity.

♻ ☆ Thermal SU(2) lattice gauge theory for intertwined orders and hole pockets in the cuprates
Harshit Pandey, Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, Ravi Shanker, Sayantan Sharma, Subir Sachdev
The cuprate pseudogap phase displays Fermi arc spectral weight in photoemission and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), while recent magnetotransport observations yield evidence for the existence of hole pockets of fractional area $p/8$, where $p$ is the doping density. We present a Monte Carlo study of a thermal SU(2) lattice gauge theory which can reconcile these observations. Our simulation includes the SU(2) gauge field $U$ of a $π$-flux spin liquid, and a SU(2) fundamental charge $e$ Higgs boson $B$. There is a Yukawa coupling between $B$, the fermionic spinons of the spin liquid, and the hole pockets of a fractionalized Fermi liquid. At the higher temperatures of the pseudogap, the finite-doping sign problem is evaded by including only thermal fluctuations of $B$ and $U$, while the fermions are diagonalized exactly for each boson background. Our study also yields a fractionalized description of intertwined orders at lower temperatures, including the onset of $d$-wave superconductivity by the expulsion of vortices with flux $h/(2e)$, each with charge-order halos. We discuss conditions under which quantum oscillations in the density of states from hole pockets of area $p/8$ could be observable in clean under-hole-doped cuprates.
comment: 33 pages, 16 figures; (v7) Updated computations on quantum oscillations (v8) added introduction on Ancilla Layer Model
♻ ☆ Fractionalized Fermi liquids and the cuprate phase diagram
Pietro M. Bonetti, Maine Christos, Alexander Nikolaenko, Aavishkar A. Patel, Subir Sachdev
We review a theoretical framework for the cuprate superconductors, rooted in a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*) description of the intermediate-temperature pseudogap phase at low doping. The FL* theory predicted hole pockets each of fractional area $p/8$ at hole doping $p$, in contrast to the area $p/4$ in spin density wave theory. Magnetotransport measurements, including observation of the Yamaji angle, show clear evidence of hole pocket quasiparticles which can tunnel coherently between square lattice layers, and are consistent with the FL* description. The FL* phase of a single-band model is described using a layer construction with a pair of ancilla qubits on each site: the Ancilla Layer Model (ALM). Fluctuations are described by the SU(2) gauge theory of a background spin liquid with critical Dirac spinons. A Monte Carlo study of the thermal SU(2) gauge theory transforms the hole pockets into Fermi arcs in photoemission. One route to confinement of FL* upon lowering temperature yields a $d$-wave superconductor via a Kosterlitz-Thouless transition of $h/(2e)$ vortices, with nodal Bogoliubov quasiparticles featuring anisotropic velocities and vortices surrounded by charge order halos. Increasing doping from the FL* phase in the ALM drives a transition to a conventional Fermi liquid (FL) at large doping, passing through an intermediate strange metal regime. We formulate a theory of the FL*-FL metal-metal transition without a symmetry-breaking order parameter, using a critical quantum `charge' liquid of mobile electrons in the presence of disorder, developed via an extension of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model to two spatial dimensions. At low temperatures, and across optimal and over doping, we address the regimes of extended non-Fermi liquid behavior by Griffiths effects near quantum phase transitions in disordered metals.
comment: 101 pages, 43 figures. Review article based on lectures by SS at Boulder, Trieste, Hong Kong, with links to lecture videos. Comments welcome. v3. Introduced terminology of Ancilla Layer Model (ALM). v4. Added additional QMC results on variable exponents in Griffiths phase; v7. Updated results on quantum oscillations
♻ ☆ Constraints on the volume enclosed by Fermi surfaces
Subir Sachdev
A fundamental property of a Fermi liquid (FL) is that the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by $ρ$, the total density of electrons. In a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*), the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by the same expression after $ρ$ has been shifted by a quantized amount, most commonly to $ρ-1$ (we assume spin rotation invariance, for simplicity). The FL* shift is related to the quantized symmetry fractionalization data of a quantum spin liquid, whose fractionalized spinon excitations are present alongside the Fermi surface quasiparticles. In this review article, we establish the FL* Fermi volume by generalizing the original Luttinger proof for FL to parton gauge theories of the quantum spin liquid and FL*. We also discuss Oshikawa's flux insertion arguments for FL, and their extension to FL*, including a discussion of gapless spin liquids.
comment: 24 pages, 5 figure. For the Special Centenary Issue of the Indian Journal of Physics, Recent Trends in Condensed Matter Physics
♻ ☆ Local moment magnon spectrum in conduction electron tunnelling
Peter Thalmeier, Alireza Akbari
The surface tunnelling spectrum of a dual system consisting of localised moments with antiferromagnetic order coupled to conduction electrons by on-site exchange interaction is investigated. In the static approximation of the local moment order it is known that magnetic band reconstruction leads to an anomalous tunnelling spectrum at the magnetic ordering vector of local moments although the latter cannot contribute directly. In this work we consider dynamic effects by including the scattering of conduction electrons from the local moment magnon excitations. They lead to self energies and renormalisation of conduction states which in turn appreciably modify the tunnelling spectrum beyond the influence of static order, interpreted as the appearance of magnon sidebands.
comment: 11 pages, 8 figures
♻ ☆ Deconfined criticality between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a nodal d-wave superconductor: a quantum Monte Carlo study
Chuang Chen, Subir Sachdev, Zi Yang Meng
We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating Néel state and the nodal $d$-wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. Both partons move in a background $π$-flux (so the electron experiences no net flux) and are coupled to a quantum fluctuating SU(2) lattice gauge field. In contrast to earlier studies directly on the electronic degrees of freedom, we find evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition at which both the Néel and $d$-wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously. We compute correlators of the spinon-chargon composite with the same quantum numbers as the electron: we find a gapless Dirac dispersion inside the $d$-wave superconductor, turning into a gapped dispersion in the antiferromagnet.
comment: 17 pages, 7 figures
♻ ☆ Type-IV 't Hooft Anomalies on the Lattice: Emergent Higher-Categorical Symmetries and Applications to LSM Systems
Tsubasa Oishi, Hiromi Ebisu
't Hooft anomalies impose fundamental constraints on quantum matter and often lead to emergent symmetry structures upon gauging. We analyze a lattice model with four global symmetries realizing a mixed anomaly described by $\sim a_1\wedge a_2\wedge a_3\wedge a_4$, where the $a_i$ denote background gauge fields for the global symmetries. Through explicit lattice gauging, we demonstrate the emergence of higher symmetry structures, including 2-group, non-invertible, and higher fusion categorical symmetries. We also provide a field theoretical understanding of these results. Applying this framework to systems with Lieb-Schultz-Mattis anomalies, obtained by promoting part of the internal symmetries to translational symmetries, we demonstrate that modulated (dipole) symmetries and non-invertible translation symmetry arise as direct counterparts of those in systems with purely internal type-IV anomalies. Importantly, we uncover a qualitatively new feature absent in previously studied modulated symmetries and non-invertible translation: their realization can become intrinsically defect-dependent. In particular, the emergent symmetry structure changes depending on whether symmetry defects are present. This work establishes a concrete lattice realization of mixed anomalies and reveals a rich structure of emergent symmetries, thereby clarifying their role in constraining quantum phases of matter.
comment: 48 pages, 17 figures, v2: Added a discussion of non-invertible translation symmetry and references
♻ ☆ Lattice Configuration Generation with a Self-Learning Diffusion Model
Akio Tomiya
We show that a diffusion model for lattice field theory can be trained by self-learning, without configurations from a separate simulation, and used as the generator of an exact Markov chain. Training starts from exact samples at $β=0$, and along a ladder of couplings the model's own chain at each coupling, weighted by the action difference, trains the score at the next. A Metropolis-Hastings test on each proposal and its noising path keeps the sampled distribution exact for any network, so that network errors affect only the acceptance and autocorrelation times. In the two-dimensional compact XY model up to $β=1$, on the high-temperature side of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition, ladders at $L=4$ and $8$ reproduce exact and reference values of the energy density and helicity modulus at every coupling, and the generator trained from $β=0$ at $L=8$ has the same acceptance as one trained on an exact chain at $β=1$. The acceptance follows the relation known from hybrid Monte Carlo, with terms set by the number of noise levels and by the network error per site, and a network trained at $L=4$ generates up to $L=16$ when the number of levels grows with the volume.
